But what if someone asks, “Why then did Romanos I give his granddaughter in marriage to Petar, the Bulgarian tsar (in 927)?” Konstantinos answers with a tirade against Romanos I, whom he calls an illiterate low-born fellow, unqualified for office.
In his polemics against both Niketas and Romanos, Konstantinos comes across as a royal snob: he labels the former “arrogant” and the latter “impudent,” likely because they aspired to positions—
position—beyond their “proper” station.
zh: 君士坦丁七世有充分理由不喜欢尼基塔斯，因为后者与拉卡佩努斯家族有关联，并参与了919–920年使罗曼努斯·拉卡佩努斯掌权的政变。
罗曼努斯随后把皇位继承人——君士坦丁七世本人——边缘化了二十四年。这位学者皇帝后来于945年独揽大权时，对此仍耿耿于怀。在《论帝国行政》中，他建议他的儿子不可把女子许配给外族人。但如果有人问，“那么为什么罗曼努斯一世把他的孙女嫁给保加尔沙皇彼得（927年）？”君士坦丁以一段针对罗曼努斯一世的激烈抨击作答，他称后者为一个不识字、出身低贱、不配任职的家伙。
在他针对尼基塔斯和罗曼努斯两人的论战中，君士坦丁以门第论人，俨然天潢贵胄的口吻：他称前者“傲慢”、后者“无礼”，大概因为他们觊觎超出自己“本分”的地位，而那正是
地位。

en: As it happens, the two men were linked by more than Konstantinos’ polemical rhetoric. The bride in question, Maria, the one given in marriage to the Bulgarian tsar, was the daughter of Romanos’ son Christophoros, and therefore the granddaughter of Niketas himself. These upstarts not only usurped power from Konstantinos, they managed to join their bloodlines to the Bulgarian royal house. Niketas was even dispatched to personally escort the Bulgarian king to Constantinople.
The point of such an alliance might have been to solidify the Lakapenos hold on power by projecting it onto the stage of international relations and thus to further sideline Konstantinos himself.
(The latter inclined toward a Frankish alliance, which is why he made an exception for Franks in his bridal policy.
) It is no wonder that Konstantinos vented against the Bulgarians too, in the
of his grandfather Basileios I (867–886) as “vain boasters” and in
as “God-hated.”

One suspects that all these accusations of “arrogance” are linked: Slav-faced social upstarts from Greece and Bulgarian pretenders to the throne were all threats to Konstantinos’ position, and so he linked them together in his ethnic polemic.
zh: 碰巧，这两个人之间的联系不止于君士坦丁的论战修辞。所说的那位新娘玛丽亚，即被嫁给保加尔沙皇的那位，是罗曼努斯的儿子克里斯托福罗斯的女儿，因此是尼基塔斯本人的外孙女。这些暴发户不仅从君士坦丁那里篡夺了权力，还同保加尔王室结了亲。尼基塔斯甚至被派去亲自护送保加尔国王到君士坦丁堡。
这场联姻可能是想借对外结盟巩固拉卡佩努斯家族对权力的控制，从而进一步排挤君士坦丁。
（后者倾向于法兰克联盟，这就是为什么他在对外联姻一事上为法兰克人破了例。
）难怪君士坦丁也向保加尔人发泄，在他祖父瓦西里一世（867–886年在位）的《传》中称他们为“爱夸耀的浮夸之徒”，在《论军区》中称他们为“上帝所憎恨的”。
凡此种种关于“傲慢”的指责，很可能彼此相关：来自希腊、斯拉夫面孔的社会暴发户，以及保加尔的皇位觊觎者，都是对君士坦丁地位的威胁，因此他在他的族群论战中把他们联系在一起。

en: The Slavicization of the Peloponnese served in the works of Konstantinos VII as a way to discredit

rivals. Conversely, Niketas’ Hellenic rhetoric might well have been one way for social upstarts from the “untamed” lands of the south to legitimate their position. He may have been a Roman of Slavic origin, like the patriarch Niketas, the chamberlain Damianos, and the rebel Thomas. Perhaps that is why he reached back to classical antiquity when he described his own origins in his letters: it was to bypass the settlement of the Slavs while advertising his embrace of upper-class Roman culture, precisely the sort of “civilization” that helped to distinguish Romans from barbarians. And perhaps that was why Konstantinos VII placed his hyperbolic statement about the Slavicization of Greece in the section of the

that is devoted to the Peloponnese, in order to set the stage for the defamation and delegitimization of his political enemy Niketas. As a Slav, Niketas would by definition have been a barbarian, “the opposite of ‘civilization’ or cultural sophistication.”
We must remember that the

is devoted to the classical and antiquarian history of the empire’s provinces. There was much that Konstantinos could have said about the Peloponnese to make it seem like a bastion of classical culture and thereby reinforce Niketas’ classical persona. Instead, we get poems about the upstart “
-face” and the Slavicization of the land.
zh: 伯罗奔尼撒的斯拉夫化在君士坦丁七世的著作中充当了一种败坏

对手名誉的方式。反过来，尼基塔斯的希腊修辞很可能是一种方式，让来自南方“未驯服”土地的新贵证明他们有资格居于如今的位置。他可能是一个斯拉夫出身的罗马人，就像牧首尼基塔斯、寝宫总管达米阿诺斯和叛乱者托马斯一样。也许这就是为什么他在书信中描述自己出身时追溯到古典时代，既可略过斯拉夫人定居的历史，也可显示自己推崇罗马上层文化，恰恰是那种有助于把罗马人与蛮族区分开来的“文明”。也许这就是为什么君士坦丁七世把他关于希腊斯拉夫化的夸张陈述放在《论军区》中专门论述伯罗奔尼撒的那一节，好为诋毁政敌尼基塔斯、质疑其地位做好铺垫。作为一个斯拉夫人，尼基塔斯按定义就会是一个蛮族，“‘文明’或文化教养的反面”。
我们必须记得，《论军区》专门论述帝国行省的古典时代的历史和旧事。关于伯罗奔尼撒，君士坦丁本可以说很多，使它看起来像古典文化的一个堡垒，从而强化尼基塔斯的古典形象。相反，人们读到的却是嘲笑暴发户长着一张“
脸”的诗句，以及这片土地斯拉夫化的说法。

en: As it happens, we can possibly dig deeper into Niketas’ background. A contemporary chronicle tells the story, set around 921, of an “uneducated” Rentakios Helladikos who, under Romanos I, was a relative of Niketas
(i.e., our

). This man is said to have attacked his father and plundered his possessions, before seeking asylum in Hagia Sophia. The emperor Romanos wanted to remove him from the church and punish him, but Rentakios sent forged letters to the Bulgarians promising to defect. We must remember in this connection that the Bulgarians under Tsar Simeon (d. 927) had recently been raiding as far south as the Gulf of Corinth. Rentakios was arrested and blinded.
zh: 尼基塔斯的家世还有一些线索可循。一部同时代编年史记载了约921年发生的一件事，主角是“没受过教育的”伦塔基奥斯·赫拉迪科斯，他在罗曼努斯一世治下是尼基塔斯
（即我们的
）的一个亲属。据说此人袭击了他的父亲并掠夺了他的财产，然后到圣索菲亚大教堂寻求庇护。皇帝罗曼努斯想让人把他带出教堂加以惩处，但伦塔基奥斯向保加尔人发送伪造的书信，承诺叛逃。在这方面我们必须记得，沙皇西美昂（卒于927年）治下的保加尔人不久前曾南下袭掠，远至科林斯湾。伦塔基奥斯被逮捕并被刺瞎。

en: The Rentakioi were a Peloponnesian family.

Helladikos was, then, a relation on Niketas’ father’s side, the “Spartan” side. The name Rentakios was of Slavic origin, though there is no proof that any people who bore it by this point spoke Slavic.

In Rentakios Helladikos’ appeal to the tsar, we note again a “sinister” connection to the Bulgarians, which his relative Niketas would solidify through an actual marriage alliance. Note also the seemingly Hellenic name
It appears, however, that its original form was
referring to the olive-oil business (these were “oily” men, not

“Helladikos” was an attempt to classicize the name, which appeared to Konstantinos VII as just more impudence. One Ioannes Eladas had been a member of the regency that had ruled in Konstantinos’ place during his minority, possibly another reason for the later emperor to dislike the family as a whole.
zh: 伦塔基奥斯家族是一个伯罗奔尼撒家族。
那么，赫拉迪科斯是尼基塔斯父系——“斯巴达”那一系——的一个亲属。伦塔基奥斯这个名字源于斯拉夫语，尽管没有证据表明到这时任何使用它的人还讲斯拉夫语。
在伦塔基奥斯·赫拉迪科斯向沙皇的求助中，我们再次注意到与保加尔人的一层“别有用心”的关系，他的亲属尼基塔斯后来还以联姻巩固了这层关系。也注意那个看似希腊的名字
（Helladikos）。然而，它最初的形式似乎是
（Eladikos），指橄榄油生意（这些是“油乎乎”的人，不是
（Hellenes）……）。
“赫拉迪科斯”是试着把这个名字改得合乎古典用语，在君士坦丁七世看来，这不过又是一种僭越。一个约安尼斯·埃拉达斯曾是君士坦丁未成年期间代他统治的摄政委员会的成员，这可能是后来这位皇帝不喜欢整个家族的另一个原因。

en: It is therefore likely that our Niketas was the same as the Niketas Eladikos
(a court title) who was sent by Zoe in 914 to negotiate with the Bulgarians over Adrianople.

This family was all too close to the Bulgarians, to say nothing of their Slavic faces and oily business. It is no wonder that Niketas sought to play up his Athenian and Spartan credentials. In one of his letters from exile, he asked the metropolitan of Kyzikos to send him some olive oil, “which this miserable place lacks.”
zh: 因此，很可能我们的尼基塔斯与身为
（protospatharios，宫廷头衔）的尼基塔斯·埃拉迪科斯是同一人。914年，佐伊曾派他就阿德里安堡与保加尔人谈判。
这个家族与保加尔人实在太近了，更不用说他们的斯拉夫面孔和油乎乎的生意。难怪尼基塔斯尽力彰显自己和雅典、斯巴达的渊源。在他一封流放期间的书信中，他请求基齐库斯都主教给他送一些橄榄油，“这个可怜的地方所缺乏的”。

en: Niketas

exemplifies how Slavic ethnicity could be attributed, covered up, or ameliorated in Romanía. It was part of a long Roman tradition of ethnicity-as-politics that stretched back to the days of the Republic.
zh: 从尼基塔斯行政长官的事例可以看到，在罗曼尼亚，斯拉夫出身可以被强加给人，也可以被掩盖或淡化。这样拿族群出身做政治文章，早在罗马共和国时代就已成为传统。

en: Conclusions
zh: 结论

en: It was generally bad for a Roman to be branded as an ethnic type. The retention of a foreign language was not something to boast about.

In politics, old ethnic affiliations could be dredged up and used against otherwise mainstream Roman rivals. In this chapter we have seen it done with Slavic and Arab ethnic origins, and we will examine the advantages and disadvantages of an Armenian ancestry in Chapter  5. But any association was fair game. The emperor Michael III insulted the patriarch Photios as a “Khazar-face.”
The empress Theophano called the chamberlain Basileios Lakapenos a Scythian and a barbarian (because of his mother).
The poet Ioannes Geometres used Slavic words to insult his enemy Psenas, imputing ethnicity to him, just as Niketas
was mocked at the court of Konstantinos VII.
A candidate for the patriarchal throne in the fourteenth century was insulted as a
a Bulgarian-Albanian-Vlach.
A textbook case would be Anna Komnene’s attack on the ethnicity of the eleventh-century philosopher Ioannes Italos.
This may have played out on the local level too, as when children threw stones at Saint Neilos for wearing what appeared to them to be a Bulgarian hat (Snapshot 8).
zh: 对一个罗马人来说，遭人扣上某种族群的帽子通常不是好事。仍然说一门外语不是值得夸耀的事。
在政治中，旧的族群归属可以被翻出来，用来对付其他方面均与普通罗马人无异的政敌。在本章中我们已经看到有人拿斯拉夫和阿拉伯出身做文章，我们将在第5章考察亚美尼亚血统的利弊。但只要沾上一点外族背景，就可以拿来攻击。皇帝米海尔三世侮辱牧首佛提乌为“哈扎尔脸”。
皇后塞奥法诺称寝宫总管瓦西里·拉卡佩努斯为斯基泰人和蛮族（因为他的母亲）。
诗人约安尼斯·格奥梅特雷斯用斯拉夫词语侮辱他的敌人普塞纳斯，硬说他是外族出身，正如尼基塔斯
在君士坦丁七世的朝廷被嘲笑一样。
十四世纪一个牧首之位的候选人被侮辱为
，即一个保加尔—阿尔巴尼亚—弗拉赫人。
一个教科书式的案例是安娜·科穆宁娜针对十一世纪哲学家约安尼斯·伊塔洛斯出身的攻击。
这种情况也可能发生在民间，例如孩子们见圣尼洛斯戴了一顶看似保加尔人的帽子，便朝他丢石头（剪影8）。

en: In many of these and other cases, it is hard to know whether there was any truth to the ethnic imputation or whether it was invented or exaggerated for polemical purposes. I suspect that in most cases this colorful language was used against men whose cultural profile was mainstream Roman, whatever their ancestry. If this was the case, many Romans would have been vulnerable when the stakes were high and the knives came out. Romanogenesis continued apace in Romanía as refugees, captives, foreign armies, and even invaders who had settled on imperial territory were taken in, absorbed, and admitted into the majority Roman group. The whole process could sometimes be accomplished during the course of a few generations, two or three if mixed marriages were involved, or longer if the foreign population was larger.

Assimilation was often messy around the edges, or incomplete, or it left visible traces. All the evidence suggests that the Romans of Byzantium disliked ethnic foreigners, but they were simultaneously willing to admit them into their polity and even their ethnicity. No groups who wished to join were excluded or turned away, even Muslim warriors who had been fighting against the empire.
zh: 在这些和其他许多案例中，很难知道这些族群出身的说法到底属实，还是出于论战而编造或夸大的。我怀疑在大多数情况下，那些尖刻的说辞，针对的多半是在文化上与大多数罗马人无异的人，无论他们的血统如何。如果是这样，利害攸关、攻讦四起之时，许多罗马人都可能因此受到攻击。罗马族源生成在罗曼尼亚迅速继续，因为难民、战俘、外族军队、甚至定居于帝国领土的入侵者陆续得到接纳，融入占多数的罗马族群。整个过程有时可以在几代人的时间内完成，如果涉及混合婚姻则是两到三代，如果外族人口更大则更长。
同化往往并不那么彻底，也并不总是顺利，有时还有迹可循。所有证据都表明，拜占庭的罗马人不喜欢族群外人，但他们同时愿意把这些人接纳进他们的政治共同体、甚至他们的族群。任何想要加入的群体都没有被排除或拒绝，甚至是曾与帝国作战的穆斯林战士。

en: Becoming Roman entailed far more than just converting to Christianity. It required learning Greek, meeting the demands of the Roman state, and adopting a new cultural and ethnic profile. The Romans expected a complete makeover of potential members of their polity. In modern terms, we would say that Romanía practiced an expansive model of assimilationist membership, trusting in its way of life and institutions such as the Church, army, legal system, and imperial court to gradually make Romans out of foreigners; it did not restrict membership to those who already belonged to the

But Romanía was not for all that a multicultural state: the Romans had zero respect for foreign cultures as such and recognized no imperative to preserve them. In some sectors of opinion today their policies might be condemned as cultural genocide, even if their openness to refugees might be praised.
zh: 成为罗马人远不止于皈依基督教。它要求学习希腊语、满足罗马国家的要求，并采纳一种新的文化和族群面貌。对希望加入罗马政治共同体的人，罗马人期待他们作出彻底的改变。用现代术语说，我们会说罗曼尼亚愿意接纳外族为共同体成员，条件是同化。它相信罗马人的生活方式和教会、军队、法律体系、朝廷等制度能逐渐把外族变成罗马人，因而愿意接纳原本不属于罗马
（genos）的人。
但尽管如此，罗曼尼亚并不是一个多元文化国家：罗马人毫不尊重外族文化本身，也不承认有任何保存它们的义务。在今天，有些人看来，他们的政策可能被谴责为文化灭绝，即使他们对难民的开放可能受到赞扬。

en: One court author described “the polity of the Romans” as “an altar of safety for refugees fleeing savagery to our civility and mildness.”

He was referring to a group of Bulgar refugees whom the court refused to return to their khan when he angrily demanded it. Many Byzantine texts claim that foreign groups who adopted Roman norms would become civilized in time. This was a proud and uninterrupted Roman conceit, dating to antiquity.
It suggests that, even if they were ethnically prejudiced, the Romans were not racists, if we define a racist as someone who believes that traits are ingrained and cannot ever change.

To be sure, some policies sparked controversy and pushback, such as Theophilos’ order that Roman women should marry Khurramite men. There must have been internal debates about the specific measures. And, as Angeliki Laiou observed, the first generation of such new Romans “remain[ed] under scrutiny, almost on probation . . . rarely assimilated fully. By the second generation, assimilation was far advanced, although some people might remember and mention the non-Roman antecedents of a family.”
zh: 一位朝廷作家把“罗马人的政治共同体”描述为“一座庇护难民的祭坛。他们逃离野蛮，前来投奔我们文明而温厚的社会”。
他指的是一群保加尔难民，朝廷拒绝把他们交还给他们的可汗，尽管可汗愤怒地要求。许多拜占庭文本声称，采纳罗马规范的外族群体会随着时间变得文明。罗马人以此自许，这种观念从古代一直延续下来。
它表明，即使罗马人有族群偏见，他们也不是种族主义者——如果我们把种族主义者定义为相信人的特征与生俱来、永远无法改变的人。
诚然，有些政策引发了争议和抵制，例如狄奥斐卢斯命令罗马妇女应嫁给胡拉米派男子。关于具体措施必定有过内部辩论。而且，正如安格利基·拉伊乌所观察到的，第一代这样的新罗马人“仍受审视，几乎处于试用期……很少完全同化。到第二代，同化程度已相当高，尽管有些人可能记得并提及一个家族的非罗马祖先”。

en: Laiou was referring to resettlements that involved intermarriage and a new Roman environment for the newcomers. But some cases did not take place under optimal conditions and did not work out, for example the Pechenegs who turned against their Roman hosts in the mid-eleventh century. The frustrated underlying expectations were then revealed: a Pecheneg leader had changed only his clothes, not his soul, complained a court orator.
And it could get racist: you can’t paint the Ethiopian white after all, said a historian at the time, noting that the Pechenegs continued their old habits of raiding the empire.
zh: 拉伊乌指的是涉及通婚和让新来者置身于罗马环境的迁置。但有些案例并非在最佳条件下发生，也没有成功，例如十一世纪中叶转而反对他们罗马东道主的佩切涅格人。于是失望之中，原先隐而未明的期待显露了出来：一个佩切涅格首领只换了衣服，心性却一点没变，一位朝廷演说家抱怨道。
这种说法也可能带上种族主义色彩：毕竟你不能把埃塞俄比亚人涂白，当时一位历史学家说，指出佩切涅格人继续他们袭掠帝国的旧习惯。

en: Integration was not always successful. Consider the divergent lives of two Turkish children. Both were taken captive in the later eleventh century and sent to the imperial court as presents. The first had been a child soldier fighting against the empire around 1080; the second was captured when Nikaia fell in 1097. They were adopted, given titles, and associated with the imperial family. But the first, Tzachas, was cut off from access to the court when Alexios I seized power, so he reverted to raiding and became the empire’s foe, temporarily conquering much of western Asia Minor.

The second, Axouch, was given by Alexios I as a playmate to his son and heir Ioannes II. He grew up to become one of the most powerful court officials and the founder of a prestigious and thoroughly Roman family.
zh: 整合并不总是成功。考虑两个突厥儿童迥异的人生。两人都在十一世纪晚期被俘，并作为礼物被送到帝国朝廷。第一个约1080年曾是一个与帝国作战的童兵；第二个在1097年尼西亚陷落时被俘。他们被收养、授予头衔，与皇室有了联系。但第一个，察哈斯，在阿莱克修斯一世夺取权力时再也无法亲近朝廷，于是重操袭掠的旧业，成为帝国的敌人，暂时征服了小亚细亚西部的大部分。
第二个，阿克苏赫，被阿莱克修斯一世安排做儿子兼继承人约安尼斯二世的玩伴。他长大后成为最有权势的朝廷官员之一，由他开创了一个显赫且完全罗马化的家族。

en: The expectation of complete Romanization harbored yet another source of potential conflict: the Romans talked about themselves as a

a kinship community, yet knew perfectly well that many among themselves had a foreign ancestry. In some cases, this did not matter and was soon forgotten or ignored, but in others it created a potential for ethnic politics and prejudice.
zh: 对完全罗马化的期望还藏着另一个潜在冲突的来源：罗马人自称一个
（genos），即由亲缘相连的共同体，却完全清楚他们中间许多人有外族血统。在某些情况下，这不要紧，很快被遗忘或忽视，但在另一些情况下，这种出身却可能沦为政治攻讦和族群偏见的由头。

en: A fascinating case study of this “melting pot” reality is provided by the advice writer of the eleventh century, Kekaumenos. He had served as a high imperial official, mostly in the Balkans, and takes considerable pride in being Roman and serving the interests of Romanía.

At one point he advises the emperors not to promote foreigners to high positions because that demeans the Romans who could have been promoted instead. He formulates this as a matter of national interest and pride: “it is not in the interests of Romanía to do this,” and “Romanía prospered when the high commands were held by Romans.” Yet elsewhere in his book of maxims he casually reveals that among his ancestors were a local lord of Dvin in Armenia (a man of unspecified ethnic background), who captured a fort in Armenia from the Roman general in command there; the latter is said to have called Kekaumenos’ ancestor “an enemy of Romanía.” He also reveals that another of his ancestors fought for the Bulgarian tsar Samuil against Basileios II during the great wars, before he switched sides. Yet another ancestor, also named Kekaumenos, had fought for Basileios against Samuil.
His mixed ancestry in no way diminished Kekaumenos’ proud Roman patriotism as expressed in his career and opinions.
zh: 十一世纪写劝诫书的凯考梅诺斯，是观察这种“熔炉”如何运作的一个有意思的例子。他曾担任高级帝国官员，主要在巴尔干，并以身为罗马人、为罗曼尼亚效力而自豪。

有一处他建议皇帝们不要把外人提拔到高位，因为那会贬低那些本可以被提拔的罗马人。他把这表述为关乎民族利益和尊严的事：“这样做不符合罗曼尼亚的利益”，以及“罗马人担任高级指挥职务时，罗曼尼亚便繁荣昌盛”。然而在他的格言集别处，他不经意地透露，他的祖先中有一个亚美尼亚德温的地方领主（一个族群背景不明的人），此人从那里指挥的罗马将军手中夺取了亚美尼亚的一座堡垒；据说后者称凯考梅诺斯的祖先为“罗曼尼亚的敌人”。他还透露，他的另一个祖先曾在几场大战期间为保加尔沙皇萨穆伊尔效力，与瓦西里二世作战，后来改投另一方。又一个祖先，也叫凯考梅诺斯，曾为瓦西里对抗萨穆伊尔作战。
多样的祖源丝毫没有减损凯考梅诺斯的罗马爱国情怀。他的仕途和言论都显示出他以此为傲。

en: I am confused by Curta’s unexplained rejection of Niketas’ Roman identity (
296n13: “He cannot be regarded as a Roman . . . never claimed to be a Roman”). This overlooks his

directly contradicts Curta’s understanding of Roman identity in Byzantium (294–295); does not consider Niketas’ career ; fails to explain what his ethnicity was if not Roman; and is a weak argument anyway: in our extant evidence, it is also likely that Scipio, Lucretius, or Vergil also did not “claim to be Romans.” As Curta himself says on the previous page, specifically with regard to Roman identity in the Byzantine provinces, “There was no need to stress the obvious” (295).
